questions.question: A React app calls `fetch("/api/payments", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(data) })` and `req.body` is undefined in Express even though `express.json()` is registered. What is the most likely cause?
options: The request has no `Content-Type: application/json` header, so the JSON parser skips it
The body is larger than 1 byte
questions.explanation: Body parsers only run when the request's Content-Type matches their `type` option. Without the JSON content type, `express.json()` ignores the request and `req.body` stays undefined.

questions.question: What happens when a client sends a 500 KB JSON body to a route behind `express.json({ limit: "100kb" })`?
options: The body is truncated to 100 KB and passed to the handler
The handler runs with `req.body` set to `null`
The request is rejected with a 413 Payload Too Large error before the handler runs
questions.explanation: When the body exceeds `limit`, the parser stops and forwards a 413 error to the error-handling middleware. The route handler never runs.

questions.question: What is the default value of the `extended` option for `express.urlencoded()` in Express 5?
options: `false`, so a simple parser without nested objects is used
`true`, so nested objects are parsed with the qs library
There is no default; omitting it throws an error
questions.explanation: Express 5 changed the default to `extended: false`. Opt into `extended: true` only when you need nested bracket syntax in form fields.

questions.question: Which multer setup is safest for a KYC document upload endpoint?
options: `multer()` with no options, trusting the browser to limit file size
Saving each file to disk using `file.originalname` as the path
Setting `limits.fileSize`, filtering allowed types in `fileFilter`, and generating your own file names
questions.explanation: Without `limits.fileSize` multer accepts any size, the client-supplied name can enable path traversal, and `express.json()` cannot parse `multipart/form-data`. Limits, type checks and server-generated names are the baseline.
